title: Tennessee Botches Execution: Christa Pike Intubated in Critical Condition After Failed Lethal Injection
snippet: Death row prisoner Christa Pike is on a ventilator after surviving two doses of pentobarbital during a botched Tennessee execution attempt, according to an emergency court filing.
content:
A botched execution attempt in Tennessee has left death row inmate Christa Pike in critical condition at a Nashville-area hospital, where she remains unconscious and on a ventilator, according to an emergency court motion filed on October 2.

Pike, 50, survived two full doses of pentobarbital on September 30 during what was supposed to be her execution for the 1996 conviction in the torture and murder of Colleen Slemmer. Court documents reveal that execution personnel failed to establish functional intravenous access, causing the lethal compound to infiltrate her tissue rather than properly enter her bloodstream. The filing notes that both of Pike's arms were left swollen, burned, and blistered from the failed procedure.

'Reckless and Incompetent' Procedure

The court motion accuses the Tennessee Department of Correction (TDOC) of a "manifest violation" of Pike's constitutional rights, calling the state's actions "reckless" and "incompetent."

"Apparently at no point did any member of the execution team realize that the IV lines were not correctly placed or that the veins had blown," the motion states. Rather than stopping to assess the situation, officials administered a second backup dose of pentobarbital while Pike was still breathing on the gurney.

Prior to the execution, Pike's legal team had warned state officials that her underlying blood disorder, thrombocytosis, presented severe risks for IV line placement. State officials dismissed those concerns at the time as speculative.

Political Fallout and State Moratorium

The unprecedented survival of a prisoner following state-administered lethal injection drugs has sparked severe political fallout. Tennessee Governor Bill Lee called the failed execution "deeply disturbing," ordered a full pause on all executions in the state for the remainder of the year, and announced an independent third-party investigation into TDOC's practices.

The move postpones the execution of death row inmate Gary Wayne Sutton, which was set for December 3. Meanwhile, political pressure is mounting against TDOC Commissioner Frank Strada, with candidates from both major parties in the state's upcoming gubernatorial election calling for his removal.

The incident marks the latest in a series of botched capital punishment procedures in Tennessee. In 2022, Governor Lee temporarily suspended executions after an independent review uncovered systemic protocol failures dating back years, including a failure to properly test lethal injection drugs for purity and potency.
